notes: How this part was researched: the session's shared web-search allowance ran out after this part's first eight searches (the legislative candidates), so everything else was found by reading pages directly with the kit's honest User-Agent (states/net.py), one request at a time, with each site's robots.txt obeyed by that reader (the lapses are listed under this part's mistakes below): the candidates' own sites, each county's, city's and school district's own site (their council minutes and directories included), the Minnesota DFL's list of endorsed candidates and local party units' pages, the Legislative Reference Library, Wikipedia's election articles, and local newspapers through their own election sections and search pages where robots.txt allows. A voter guide (theballotbrief.com) and the University of Minnesota's election archive were read for leads only and are not cited. Likely campaign and party-unit addresses were tried by asking only whether the name has an address on the network; a campaign site (madalynnforep.com) and a candidate's personal site (www.shauncarlson.com, which links to his campaign site) were found that way and then read.

The campaign websites the candidates filed were learned from a scratch copy of the database on which the kit's own step (python -m ballot.local_sites files) had been run; the real database was only read. Each filed site was opened and read before it was listed here. Two more campaign sites were found and read: Madalynn Gerold's (the Senate District 49 DFL's candidates page links to it from her name) and Shaun Carlson's (his personal site's City Council page links to it as his campaign website).

Not read, and nothing worked around: the Minnesota Judicial Branch's site (HTTP 403 with a bot check, to the kit's reader and to the fetch tool), the state's mn.gov pages (a Radware CAPTCHA; not asked again), ballotpedia.org (a bot check), DuckDuckGo's HTML page (allowed by its robots.txt, asked once, showed a bot check), the search pages of the Thief River Falls Times and the Pine Knot News (403), the search pages of the Worthington Globe and the Waseca County Pioneer (robots.txt), Becker County's site (its certificate chain could not be verified), and the Arlington Enterprise's story on the Sibley County sheriff's race (a paywall after the first lines). So the two judges, Dannia L. Edwards and Tammy L. Merkins, have no findings.

This part's mistakes, with nothing kept from them: (1) the City of St. Michael's and the City of Detroit Lakes' sites ask unlisted scripts to stay out in robots.txt; the kit's reader stopped there, but their council pages were then opened with the fetch tool before it was settled that a stay-out applies to every reader. Nothing read there is kept (Tom Hamilton's and Ryan Gleason's council seats rest on the Press & News instead, and Shaun Carlson has no official page), and the two sites should not be asked again. (2) One InForum story and one search page on twincities.com were opened with the kit's reader before it was noticed that those sites' robots.txt turns Claude's own agents away; nothing is cited from either. (3) Wikipedia's search interface (the api.php address the kit's profile loader also uses) was asked eight questions, although robots.txt does not open /w/ to scripts; the one Wikipedia page cited below was read at its ordinary /wiki/ address. (4) The GDELT open news index was asked five questions (three were refused as too many); nothing is cited from it.

For the second reader: (a) Bonnie Westlin is a sitting member whose roster record has no birth date, so the Legislative Reference Library's is given, as parts 0, 1 and 10 did. (b) Where one page shows that an office is held and another gives the year it began or ended, the finding's url is the first page and the second page's address is written out in the source text (Ryan Dunlap, Dave Hallback, Tom Hamilton, Ryan Gleason, Mike Kuhle, Michael Polehna). A from that reads 'elected 2020' is an election year, not a start year. (c) Dave Hallback: the Pine Knot News says he 'served as Cloquet's mayor from 2014-2018'; the city's own minutes show his oath on January 6, 2015 and his successor's on January 2, 2019, and the minutes' years are the ones recorded. (d) Mike Kuhle: three stretches of service, all from the City of Worthington's council minutes. No page read says in so many words that the Ward 2 member seated on November 12, 2024 is the former mayor; the tie is the same name on the same council, which is the body he is running for. (e) Tom Hamilton: the newest page read that calls him a council member is the Press & News story of May 21, 2026 ('Councilmember Tom Hamilton'); with the four-year term he was sworn into on January 14, 2025, his 'to' is given as now, and the second reader may prefer to leave it empty. Ryan Gleason's rests on the same paper's September 17, 2026 voter's guide ('incumbent Ryan Gleason'). (f) Sally Lorberbaum's three appointed posts come from her campaign site, which gives lengths of service and no years. (g) Madalynn Gerold: her own site and Eden Prairie Local News say she ran for the Minnesota House in 2018 without naming a party; Wikipedia's results table gives the party and district (the University of Minnesota's election archive agrees). The birth date that archive shows was not taken, because the source it names is a birth records index. (h) Peter M Fischer's campaign site still shows a 2024 copyright line and a 2024 endorsements page; its home page announces the run for re-election in House District 44A without a year.

party_support (a key the loader does not read, in the shape parts 0, 6 and 10 use): the Senate District 49 DFL names Madalynn Gerold under 'Local Candidates we support', a heading that is not the word endorsement (part 10 records the same page for another candidate in her race). It is kept apart from endorsed_by so that no page calls it an endorsement; whether and how it is shown is John's decision.

For whoever holds race 2026-MN-1010-17486 (East Bethel Council Member, At Large): the City of East Bethel's own notice of August 6, 2026 says Council Member Tim Miller, who is on our November list, died on August 1, 2026 after filing, and that his name will still be printed on the city's ballots. It is written as a review item under Mark Duchene, the candidate of that race in this part, although it is not about him. ABC Newspapers reported on August 13, 2026 that the council appointed Dino Perfetti to hold the seat until the candidate elected in November takes office; the same paper's list of candidates (compiled with AI assistance, by its own note) also names Perfetti as a candidate, which our list, the Secretary of State's, does not.

No Republican party page with a 2026 endorsement of Keri Heintzeman was found: the Republican Party of Minnesota's '2026 Republican Nominees' pages list statewide and congressional candidates only, the Itasca County Republicans' site lists her under 'Our Legislators' without the word endorsed, and no site was found for the Crow Wing or Cass County units.

Nothing a card may show was found for Terry Strege, Jacob Vold, Ty Backlund, Denley Kompelien, Mark Duchene, Aaron Sinclair, Cara McClincy, Nikki Gieseke and the two judges. Read for them: Wright County's news posts on the commissioner races and KRWC's May 14, 2026 story (Strege; the story says he lost the same seat's 2022 election, a nonpartisan run); Traverse County's commissioner, city-official and township-officer pages (Vold is on none); WTIP's January 23 and September 30, 2026 stories (Backlund); East Bethel's council and commission pages (Duchene is on none); the Little Falls district's board page and the Morrison County Record's election coverage (Sinclair is not on the board; the paper's July 27 filing story predates his filing); the Hermantown district's own '2026 School Board Candidates' page, which carries McClincy's introduction and names no public office; the Owatonna district's board and election pages (Gieseke is not on the board; the district's campaign-finance list shows she also ran in 2022 and 2024, nonpartisan runs). What those pages say of work, schools and household is not recorded. Ages and graduation years were not turned into birth years.
